dispositions.rationale: The runner write log is the named evidence; a log that omits a write is the same attestation problem as a report that lies about its model, and the tree cannot see past either.
A case pass or fail is its lock (ACE-D7, ACE-D8); there is no separate outcome store for an experiment to touch.
Isolation joins the fields ARM-A6 checks; the orchestrator arm runs in the authoring context, the subagent arm fresh, both recorded on the dispatch.
A self-check run records the criteria before and after the self-check, and the scorer refuses one lacking both.
Same; isolation under ARM-A6.
A plan whose objection set holds an objection without a decision is refused.
A plan whose arm 2 ledger lacks a rationale is refused.
For arm 3 the adjudication record must hold the held-out objections listed and none adjudicated.
Same.
The report gives the held-out count for arm 3.
Writing the plan before dispatch rests on the operator, as ARM-D3 states; nothing in the committed tree can observe it.
Committing every run rests on the operator, as ARM-D3 states; nothing in the committed tree can observe it.
The runner write log is the named evidence; a log that omits a write is the same attestation problem as a report that lies about its model, and the tree cannot see past either.
Inputs are stripped of any field naming a lens, arm or model.
An unplanned repeat matches nothing under ARM-A7 and leaves no usable report the scorer reads; the tree sees only committed reports, and the plan fixes the count.

ARM-D2: a held-out objection reaches the adjudicator as a listed repeat, so a seeded wrong rejection listed counts as reaching adjudication for overturnability, while counting in neither repeats nor effort.
The plan fixes each arm prompt from the emitter at plan time; the scorer compares the run to the plan, not to the emitter later.
Same.
Usable reports match the plan one to one; a repeat superseded reports match nothing.
The held-out count is reported for arm 3.
A plan whose run-id a committed run already holds is refused; ARM-D3 gives one run-id per run.

parts.statement: The evaluation of record's locks are identical before and after an experiment.
Experiment scores remain separate from the evaluation of record and change no case's pass or fail.

obligations.source: Problem statement: "The experiments' results are therefore scored apart from it, and they change no case's pass or fail." ARM-D3: "the evaluation of record's locks are the same before and after it."
obligations.statement: The experiments remain separate from the evaluation of record and preserve its decisions and locks.

parts.statement: Orchestrator authoring occurs in the context holding the objections and decisions.
The orchestrator self-check performs the specified read and edits before attack in that same context.
The subagent authors and performs the specified self-check in a fresh context containing only the prescribed inputs.

obligations.source: ARM-D1: "The orchestrator authors the criteria in the context that holds the objections and decisions." The self-check is "one read ... against ... one-obligation, observable-obligation and consistency rules, with edits, before the attack"; the orchestrator uses "the same context" and the subagent uses "a fresh context given only the document, the objections with their decisions, and the standard."
obligations.statement: The authoring arms execute the distinct authoring and self-check processes defined in ARM-D1.

parts.statement: The runs use the planned pinned document and fixed objection set, one planned model, three authoring results per arm, and the required full-panel attack counts and membership.
The fixed authoring objection set consists of accepted objections accompanied by the author's decisions.

obligations.source: ARM-D1: "Each arm gets one document at a pinned revision and one fixed set of accepted objections with the author's decisions. Each authors three times with one model named in the run plan. The full panel attacks each result once ..."
obligations.statement: Authoring uses controlled inputs, three repetitions with one planned model, and one full-panel attack per result.

parts.statement: The scorer counts exactly those two classes of introduced defect, counting an objection in both classes once.

obligations.source: ARM-D1: "An introduced defect is either of two things" followed by a valid objection targeting an added or changed criterion and "an accepted objection the result leaves unanswered."
obligations.statement: Introduced defects are valid objections targeting added or changed criteria and accepted objections left unanswered.

parts.statement: An arm ranks ahead exactly at a difference of at least three defects across three results; smaller differences are reported as no difference.
An arm with fewer than three results or a pending result ranks nowhere.

obligations.source: ARM-D1: "An arm ranks ahead when, and only when, its three results carry at least three fewer introduced defects in total. A smaller difference is no difference. An arm with fewer than three results ranks nowhere."
obligations.statement: Authoring rankings use the specified total-defect threshold and exclude incomplete arms.

parts.statement: Arms 1 and 3 use the document-only panel prompt under the required configuration.
Arm 2 receives a ledger of earlier rejected grounds with their rationales.
Arm 3 holds every objection matched to an earlier rejected ground out of adjudication before adjudication occurs.
Every held-out objection is preserved and listed to the adjudicator as a repeat with its matched ground.

obligations.source: ARM-D2's arm list: "the document only"; "the document with a ledger of earlier rejected grounds and their rationales"; and document-only with a post-filter that holds matched objections out before adjudication and lists them "as a repeat, with the ground it matched; nothing is dropped."
obligations.statement: The re-attack arms expose the specified information and apply the specified post-filter.

parts.statement: Each fixture names a committed PR 791 attack record and contains at least one ledger-rejected ground with a judge validity ruling.
Each arm has five planned and matching full-panel runs per fixture with the required panel membership.

obligations.source: ARM-D2: "Fixtures are re-attack rounds from the history of PR 791 ... each with at least one seeded wrong rejection." A seed is "a ground the judge has ruled valid and the ledger marks rejected." "Each arm runs the full panel five times per fixture ..."
obligations.statement: Re-attack fixtures come from PR 791, contain qualifying seeded wrong rejections, and receive five full-panel runs per arm.

parts.statement: Repeats count adjudicated objections matched to earlier rejected grounds; effort counts every adjudicated objection.
Recall measures the share reaching adjudication of valid objections accepted in a later round and raised in no earlier round.
Overturnability records whether each seeded wrong rejection reaches adjudication in each run.

obligations.source: ARM-D2's "Per run, the scorer counts" list defines repeats, recall, overturnability and effort. The preceding paragraph says a held-out objection "counts in neither repeats nor effort."
obligations.statement: Per-run repeats, recall, overturnability and effort use ARM-D2's adjudication-based definitions.

parts.statement: Arm 2 or 3 meets the bar exactly when all three thresholds hold and none of its fixtures is pending.

obligations.source: ARM-D2: mean repeats are "at most half of arm 1's"; mean recall is "at most ten percentage points below arm 1's"; and every seed reaches adjudication "in at least four of five runs." ARM-D3: "an arm with a pending fixture meets no bar."
obligations.statement: The report applies the specified bar to arms 2 and 3.

parts.statement: The report uses the scorer's counts and gives repeats, recall and effort per fixture and as means over valued fixtures, seed-level overturnability run counts, and bar outcomes.
The report gives the held-out count beside repeats and effort.

obligations.source: ARM-D2: "The report gives each arm's measures per fixture and as means over the fixtures that have a value," seed overturnability as run counts, and which arms meet the bar. Earlier: "the report gives the held-out count beside" repeats and effort.
obligations.statement: The re-attack report presents fixture measures, aggregates, seed-level overturnability, bar outcomes and held-out counts.

parts.statement: No arm is named as selected or as the expected default, regardless of the measures.

obligations.source: ARM-D2: "The report selects no arm and presumes none."
obligations.statement: The re-attack report selects and presumes no arm.

parts.statement: The plan is written before experiment dispatch.
The plan contains every required configuration part and the run set matches its prescribed fields one to one.

obligations.source: ARM-D3: "The plan is written before dispatch" and fixes each arm and process, document revision, objection set, model, fixtures, seeds and validity rulings, and run counts.
obligations.statement: A complete experiment plan exists before dispatch and fixes the specified configuration.

parts.statement: Every run is committed with its plan and reports under evals/experiments/<run-id>/.
Every actual experiment write stays under evals/experiments/<run-id>/.

obligations.source: ARM-D3: "Every run is committed with its plan and reports under evals/experiments/<run-id>/, and an experiment writes nowhere else ..."
obligations.statement: Every run is committed with its plan and reports in its run directory, and the experiment writes nowhere else.

parts.statement: Runs with mismatched model, effort, transport, judge model, panel judge prompt digest or panel prompt configuration are refused.

obligations.source: The scoring-contract header identifies "the scorer, judge and configuration these experiments run under." ARM-D3: "The scorer, the judge and the lens configuration are the evaluation contract's ... and a run recorded under another does not count."
obligations.statement: Only runs using the evaluation contract's scorer, judge and lens configuration count.

parts.statement: The validity, ground-matching and incorporation tasks receive their respective prescribed inputs and use calibrated prompts for their respective questions.
Each task prompt has a passing calibration record for its digest, the panel uses the contract's judge prompt digest, and usable verdicts are yes or no with a reason.
The judge sees no arm, lens or model identifier.

obligations.source: ARM-D3's validity, ground-matching and incorporation task definitions; "Each returns yes or no with a reason, and the judge sees no arm, lens or model." "Each task has its own prompt, calibrated and digested on its own ..."
obligations.statement: The three added judge tasks use the specified inputs and questions, calibrated task prompts, reasoned binary verdicts and blinded presentation.

parts.statement: The runner plans no third repeat after two unsuccessful repeats.
The runner actually executes no more than two repeats of an unusable run.
An input still missing after the repeat limit is pending; the report names and excludes pending inputs from every measure and excludes affected arms from ranking or bar success.

obligations.source: ARM-D3: "A run with no usable report is repeated at most twice." A still-missing fixture or result is pending, omitted from every measure and named; pending results prevent ranking and pending fixtures prevent meeting the bar.
obligations.statement: Unusable runs receive at most two repeats, and missing inputs remain named and excluded from measures, rankings and bar success.

parts.statement: A fixture with no qualifying new valid objection has no recall value and is excluded from every arm's mean recall.
When no fixture has a recall value, the report states that recall cannot be judged and names no arm as meeting the bar.

obligations.source: ARM-D2: means use "fixtures that have a value." "When no fixture has a recall value, the report states that the recall condition cannot be judged, and no arm meets the bar."
obligations.statement: Missing recall values are excluded, and a wholly unjudgeable recall condition prevents every arm from meeting the bar.

ground.reason: ARM-D3 promises that an experiment "writes nowhere else" than evals/experiments/<run-id>/. ARM-A8 checks that the runner's write log names no outside path and that the evaluation locks remain unchanged. Neither check establishes that the log captures every actual write.

objections.objection: ARM-A8 lets an experiment write outside its permitted directory if the runner omits that write from its log and leaves the evaluation locks unchanged.
objections.obligation: An experiment writes only under evals/experiments/<run-id>/.

scenario.expect: ARM-A8 passes because every logged path is inside the experiment directory and the locks are unchanged, while the outside file demonstrates that write confinement is absent.
scenario.given: A runner logs its report writes under evals/experiments/<run-id>/ but also writes an unlogged scratch file elsewhere in the repository without changing any evaluation lock.
scenario.when: Acceptance checks inspect the runner's write log and compare the evaluation locks before and after the run.

ground.reason: The problem statement promises that experiment scores remain separate and change no case's pass or fail. ARM-A8 checks lock equality, which does not establish either promise.

objections.objection: The experiment can feed its results into case pass/fail decisions while leaving the evaluation locks unchanged.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but an experiment result changes a case's pass/fail outcome without changing a lock.
scenario.given: The evaluation keeps case outcomes separately from its locks, and all experiment reports satisfy the scoring criteria.
scenario.when: The experiment's scores are also used to update a case outcome.

ground.reason: ARM-D1 requires orchestrator authoring in the context holding the objections and decisions. ARM-A7 checks the plan and matching run fields, without checking that authoring context.

objections.objection: An orchestrator arm can author in a different context while its recorded run configuration matches the plan.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the orchestrator authors without the context holding the objections and decisions.
scenario.given: A complete plan names the required orchestrator process and all run fields match it.
scenario.when: The runner performs authoring in a separate context and records the planned arm and prompt.

ground.reason: ARM-D1 defines the self-check as one read against three named rules, with edits before attack, in the orchestrator's existing context. No criterion observes those actions.

objections.objection: The orchestrator self-check arm can skip its self-check and still pass every criterion.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but no required read or edit occurs before the attack.
scenario.given: The plan specifies the orchestrator self-check process and the required runs and panel.
scenario.when: The runner sends each authored result directly to the panel while retaining the planned run metadata.

ground.reason: ARM-D1 requires the subagent to author and self-check in a fresh context containing only the document, objections with decisions, and standard. Matching an arm prompt does not establish context freshness or execution of the self-check.

objections.objection: The subagent arm can use inherited context or omit its self-check.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the subagent has prior campaign context and performs no self-check.
scenario.given: The plan and recorded arm prompt contain the prescribed inputs.
scenario.when: A subagent with inherited conversation history authors the result and immediately dispatches its attack.

ground.reason: ARM-D1 requires a fixed set of accepted objections with the author's decisions. ARM-A7 checks objection-set agreement with the plan, without requiring that set to contain accepted objections and their decisions.

objections.objection: A consistently planned objection set can omit author decisions or include objections that were never accepted.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but authoring uses an objection set that does not satisfy ARM-D1.
scenario.given: A plan fixes an objection set containing an unresolved objection without an author decision.
scenario.when: Every arm uses that same set and the scorer verifies exact agreement with the plan.

ground.reason: ARM-D2 requires arm 2 to receive earlier rejected grounds with their rationales. ARM-A6 permits a ledger addition, and ARM-A7 checks prompt agreement with the plan, but neither checks that the ledger supplies those rationales.

objections.objection: Arm 2 can run with a ledger that omits the rationales it is meant to expose.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but arm 2 sees rejected grounds without their rationales.
scenario.given: The plan fixes an arm 2 prompt whose ledger lists rejected grounds and a qualifying seeded wrong rejection, but omits the rejection rationales.
scenario.when: The panel runs with that prompt and the scorer accepts the ledger addition and plan agreement.

ground.reason: ARM-D2 requires arm 3 to hold matched objections out before adjudication. ARM-A10 checks counts against the adjudication record, without requiring the post-filter to produce that record.

objections.objection: Arm 3 can adjudicate matched repeats instead of holding them out.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but matched repeats reach adjudication in arm 3.
scenario.given: An arm 3 run produces objections the judge matches to earlier rejected grounds.
scenario.when: The runner adjudicates all objections and the scorer correctly counts them from that record.

ground.reason: ARM-D2 says held-out objections are listed to the adjudicator as repeats with their matched grounds and that nothing is dropped. No criterion checks that listing or preservation.

objections.objection: Held-out objections can disappear without being listed to the adjudicator.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the adjudicator receives neither the held-out objections nor their matched grounds.
scenario.given: Arm 3 correctly holds matched objections out of adjudication.
scenario.when: The runner discards them and reports the required measures from the remaining adjudication record.

ground.reason: ARM-D2 requires the report to give the held-out count beside repeats and effort. ARM-A2 and ARM-A10 require only the four adjudication-based measures.

objections.objection: The re-attack report can omit the held-out count.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the report gives no held-out count beside repeats and effort.
scenario.given: Arm 3 holds several objections out of adjudication.
scenario.when: The report publishes repeats, recall, overturnability, effort, aggregates and bar outcomes without the held-out count.

ground.reason: ARM-D3 requires the plan to be written before dispatch. ARM-A7 checks plan contents and run agreement, without observing that ordering.

objections.objection: A plan can be reconstructed after the runs finish.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the experiment was dispatched before its plan existed.
scenario.given: The runner has completed runs with the required inputs, counts and configurations.
scenario.when: The author writes a complete matching plan afterward and submits it with the run set.

ground.reason: ARM-D3 requires every run to be committed with its plan and reports under the experiment directory. ARM-A8 checks logged paths and locks, without requiring a commit.

objections.objection: The experiment can finish with its runs, plan and reports uncommitted.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but no commit contains the run with its plan and reports.
scenario.given: All required experiment artifacts exist under the correct directory and all scoring checks pass.
scenario.when: The runner leaves those artifacts as untracked or uncommitted files.

ground.reason: ARM-D3 promises that an experiment writes nowhere outside its run directory. ARM-A8 observes the write log, which establishes only what the log names.

objections.objection: An unlogged write outside the run directory can pass the write-log criterion.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the experiment writes an artifact outside its permitted directory.
scenario.given: The runner's log contains only paths under evals/experiments/<run-id>/ and the evaluation locks remain unchanged.
scenario.when: A subprocess writes an additional report elsewhere without adding that write to the log.

ground.reason: ARM-D3 says the judge sees no arm, lens or model. ARM-A12 restricts input objects, without requiring identifying fields inside those objects to be removed.

objections.objection: The judge can see identifying metadata inside an otherwise permitted objection.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the judge sees the objection's lens identifier.
scenario.given: An objection contains a lens field and the task prompt has a passing calibration record.
scenario.when: The scorer supplies exactly the rule text and that objection to the validity task, with nothing else.

ground.reason: ARM-D3 bounds actual repeats at two. ARM-A11 prohibits planning a third repeat, which does not prohibit executing an unplanned repeat.

objections.objection: The runner can execute a third repeat while its plan and reported run set remain compliant.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the runner executes more than two repeats.
scenario.given: A run and its two repeats produce no usable report, and the plan contains no third repeat.
scenario.when: The runner executes an unplanned third repeat, discards its output, and reports the input as pending.

ground.reason: ARM-D2's arm-3 post-filter holds out of adjudication every new objection the ground-matching task matches to an earlier rejected ground. A seeded wrong rejection is, by definition, a ground the ledger marks rejected, so any re-raised seeded ground is exactly what the filter holds out. ARM-A3 (via ARM-D2's third bar condition) requires every seeded wrong rejection to reach adjudication in at least four of five runs. In the circumstance where the calibrated matcher works, the filter rule and the bar condition cannot both be satisfied: the filter succeeding makes the overturnability condition fail. The set is consistent only in the degenerate reading where arm 3 passes the bar precisely when its matcher malfunctions, which also makes arm 3's repeats count structurally zero and the repeats condition vacuous for it.

objections.objection: The criteria let through a report in which arm 3 can never meet the bar whenever its post-filter works as specified, and can meet it only when the ground-matching judge fails to match a seeded wrong rejection — rewarding matcher failure and rendering ARM-A3's 'arm 2 or arm 3' disjunction vacuous for arm 3.

scenario.expect: The filter holds the objection out of adjudication as a repeat, so the seeded wrong rejection reaches adjudication in zero of five runs; judged against ARM-A3, arm 3 fails the bar — while the same matching behaviour is what the filter rule requires, so correct behaviour and the bar condition demand incompatible outcomes.
scenario.given: A fixture whose ledger contains a seeded wrong rejection, and an arm-3 run in which a new objection re-raises that seeded ground and the calibrated ground-matching task correctly matches it to the rejected ledger entry
scenario.when: the arm-3 post-filter runs before adjudication and the scorer then evaluates ARM-D2's third bar condition (overturnability)

ground.reason: ARM-A6 refuses a run whose emitted prompt differs from 'the ac-attack emitter's current output for the same document', but 'current' has no pinned moment. The decision it leaves open is whether the emitter's output is pinned at plan time (when ARM-D3 fixes the arm prompts) or read at scoring time. Each reading produces a different outcome for the same run whenever the emitter changes between dispatch and scoring.

objections.objection: The criteria let through two scorers that reach opposite verdicts on the same run set: one refuses a run that matched the emitter at dispatch time because the emitter has since changed, the other accepts it against the plan-time emitter output.

scenario.expect: Under the scoring-time reading of 'current' the run is refused (naming the prompt difference) and its fixture goes pending; under the plan-time reading the run is accepted and counts — materially different reports from identical inputs.
scenario.given: An experiment planned and dispatched with arm prompts matching the ac-attack emitter's output at dispatch time, after which the emitter is updated so its output for the same document changes, with the run otherwise conforming
scenario.when: the scorer applies ARM-A6's emitted-prompt check

ground.reason: The set never asks what happens when an unchanged run is scored again after the ac-attack emitter changes; ARM-A6 compares against the emitter's current output, so external drift can invalidate a run that matches its plan.

objections.objection: An unchanged experiment run can be refused because the emitter moved between dispatch and scoring; no criterion pins the emitter revision or prompt digest in the plan.

scenario.expect: The run is judged against the plan-pinned prompt or a recorded emitter digest, not the emitter's newer current output
scenario.given: A planned run whose arm prompt matched the ac-attack emitter at dispatch time
scenario.when: The emitter is updated before scoring and the scorer re-evaluates the unchanged run

ground.reason: The failure path and the runs-twice case collide: ARM-A11 allows up to two repeats of a run with no usable report, but ARM-A7 refuses any run set that is not one-to-one with the plan, and no criterion says whether a repeat replaces the planned run or is an extra run.

objections.objection: A legitimately repeated run can make the committed run set differ from the plan and be refused, because the criteria do not say which attempt counts as the planned run.

scenario.expect: The repeat is matched to the planned run as a replacement, or the plan explicitly accounts for attempts, so the run set is not refused for the repeat alone
scenario.given: A planned run whose first committed report is unusable
scenario.when: The runner repeats it under ARM-A11 and both attempts are committed

ground.reason: The post-filter case is not asked of the report criteria: ARM-D2 requires the held-out count beside repeats and effort for arm 3, but ARM-A2 checks only repeats, recall, effort and overturnability.

objections.objection: An arm 3 report can omit the held-out count entirely and still satisfy every acceptance criterion, hiding how many objections the post-filter intercepted.

scenario.expect: The report gives the held-out count beside repeats and effort, as ARM-D2 states
scenario.given: Arm 3 fixture runs in which the post-filter holds objections out of adjudication
scenario.when: The re-attack report is produced

ground.reason: The concurrent case is unasked for run storage: ARM-A8 constrains writes to evals/experiments/<run-id>/ but no criterion requires run-id uniqueness or says what happens when two runs share one.

objections.objection: Two runs dispatched with the same run-id can interleave writes in one directory and each still pass ARM-A8's write-log check while corrupting each other's reports.

scenario.expect: The runner or scorer refuses the duplicate run-id, or guarantees the runs are isolated
scenario.given: Two planned experiment runs assigned the same <run-id>
scenario.when: They execute concurrently and both write only under evals/experiments/<run-id>/
